title: The film Aýna recommended
goal: Name the doer inside a clause with the genitive, and read about a favourite book.

intro.text: When the doer is a noun, it goes in the genitive and the noun at the end takes **its**: *Aýnanyň okan kitaby* (the book Aýna read), *kakamyň işleýän ýeri* (the place where my father works). When the noun at the end is the doer, neither: *kitaby okan gyz* (the girl who read the book).

why.2: The noun comes last: *Aýnanyň okan kitaby*.

exercises.title: Iň gowy görýän kitabym
exercises.passage:
Geçen ýyl Mähriniň enesi oňa bir köne kitap berdi. Bu Mollanepesiň “Zöhre-Tahyr” dessanydy. Mähri ilki ony okamak islemedi: kitabyň dili kyn ýalydy. Ýöne bir gün enesiniň okan setirlerini diňläp, ol dessanyň örän owadandygyny bildi.

Indi bu dessan Mähriniň iň gowy görýän kitaby. Ol Zöhre bilen Tahyryň söýgüsi barada okamagy halaýar. Ýöne ol joralaryna dessanyň ahyrynda näme bolýandygyny aýtmaýar: joralarynyň kitaby okamagyny isleýär.

glossary.en: epic, a long tale in verse and prose
Zöhre and Tahyr, an epic love story retold by Mollanepes

exercises.translation: Last year Mähri's grandmother gave her an old book. It was Mollanepes's epic Zöhre-Tahyr. At first Mähri didn't want to read it: the book's language seemed hard. But one day, listening to the lines her grandmother read, she realized the epic was very beautiful. Now this epic is Mähri's favourite book. She likes reading about the love of Zöhre and Tahyr. But she doesn't tell her friends what happens at the end of the epic: she wants her friends to read the book.

questions.explain: *Mähriniň enesi oňa bir köne kitap berdi.*

options: the lines she read to her grandmother
questions.explain: The genitive *enesiniň* is the doer; *setirleri*, with **its**, is what she read.

questions.q: What doesn't Mähri tell her friends?
questions.explain: *dessanyň ahyrynda näme bolýandygyny aýtmaýar*: what happens at the end.
